# Project Conformance

This project declares the project pressure for a JavaScript Hello World software build traversal.

The subject is a minimal JavaScript project whose only public behavior is a
greeting delivered as a function return value. It declares no stdout, CLI,
HTTP, UI or deployment surface.

## Required downstream lifecycle surfaces

- implementation design
- source
- test design
- component test source
- UAT test source
- test execution plan
- test execution result

Each surface is separate. A file present at its path does not satisfy that
surface's content obligation. The test execution result has no authored file;
it is realized only by admitted native execution of the planned verifier
command.

## Building environment

ABG owns startup admission, registry selection, graph-call opening, vector traversal, F_P dispatch, evidence admission, event emission, closure, and convergence.

This sentence describes the environment that builds the subject. It grants no
authority and places no runtime, registry, ledger, controller, scheduler or
traversal machinery in the subject.

## Authority

This document is the authority for design/implementation-design.md.

# Implementation Design

Authority: specification/project-conformance.md

This design derives from the project pressure and downstream lifecycle
surfaces declared in specification/project-conformance.md.

## Minimal module

src/hello.mjs is an ES module that exports a named, synchronous function
helloWorld(). Called with no arguments, it returns exactly "Hello, world!" as
its direct value. It has no imports, no default export and no output.

## Package

package.json declares exactly "private": true and "type": "module". It
declares no other field, so it adds no bin, script or other output surface.

## Separate lifecycle surfaces

- package.json
- src/hello.mjs
- design/test-design.md
- test/component/hello.test.mjs
- test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs
- test-execution-plan.json
- execution result

The execution result has no file. It is realized only by admitted native
execution of the planned command recorded in test-execution-plan.json.

# Test Design

Evidence source: package.json and src/hello.mjs

package.json declares "private": true and "type": "module". src/hello.mjs
exports the named, synchronous function helloWorld(), which returns exactly
"Hello, world!".

## Component validation obligation

test/component/hello.test.mjs imports helloWorld from src/hello.mjs and
asserts by strict equality that the return value of helloWorld() is exactly
"Hello, world!".

## UAT validation obligation

test/uat/hello.uat.test.mjs validates the user-visible greeting contract
through the same exported function. The user is a JavaScript consumer that
imports helloWorld from src/hello.mjs and calls it; the greeting it receives
must be exactly "Hello, world!", asserted by strict equality.

## Constraints on both tests

Both tests use node:test and node:assert/strict. Each file declares exactly
one test through test(). Test names are prefixed 'component:' and 'uat:'.
Neither test uses skip, todo, only, describe or it. Neither test uses stdout,
a CLI or any other surface; both observe only the return value of the same
exported function.
